headline: Approved 25 Bow Street frontage waiver and plan; continued 57 Wharf Street, 440 Highland Avenue, 56 Margin Street, and 75 North Street.
summary: The board approved a frontage waiver and an ANR plan for 25 Bow Street. It continued several other applications to later meetings, including 75 North Street by a 7-1 vote. It also referred 59 Boston to the Design Review Board.
decisions: Continued 57 Wharf Street Units UCB and UCC, and 201 Derby Street, to September 17, 2026, by a 7-0 roll call vote with one abstention.
Continued 440 Highland Avenue to October 15, 2026, by an 8-0 roll call vote.
Continued 56 Margin Street, 54 Margin Street, 7 High Street, 20 Endicott Street, and 24 Endicott Street to September 17, 2026, by a 7-0 roll call vote with one abstention.
Approved the decision with changes on the frontage waiver for 25 Bow Street, by a 7-0 roll call vote with one recusal.
Approved the decision with changes on the ANR plan for 25 Bow Street, by a 7-0 roll call vote with one recusal.
Continued 59 Boston to September 17, 2026, by an 8-0 roll call vote.
Referred 59 Boston to the Design Review Board, by an 8-0 roll call vote.
Continued 75 North Street to September 17, 2026, by a 7-1 roll call vote.
Approved the draft minutes from the July 23, 2026 regular meeting, by an 8-0 roll call vote.

MEETING AGENDA 
 
A public hearing of the Salem Planning Board and the Design Review Board was held on

Vice Chair Sarah Tarbet  calls the meeting to order at 6:31 p.m.

C. 56 Margin Street, 54 Margin Street, 7 High Street, 20 Endicott Street (Map 25, 
Lot 597), 24 Endicott Street (Map 25, Lot 595)  
Applicant: Harborlight Homes and Lifebridge North Shore  
Description: A continuation of a public hearing for all persons interested in the 
application of Harborlight Homes and Lifebridge North Shore at 56, 54 Margin 
Street, 20 Endicott Street, 7 High Street (Map 25, Lot 597) and 24 Endicott Street 
(Map 25, Lot 595) in the Residential Two-Family District (R2), Coastal Resilience 
Overlay District (C-ROD), Flood Hazard Overlay District (FHOD), and Smart 
Growth Overlay District (SGOD) for Smart Growth Overlay Plan Review and 
Coastal Resilience Overlay Site Plan Review in accordance with the following 
sections of the Salem Zoning Ordinance: Section 7.4 Smart Growth Overlay 
District and Section 8.9 Coastal Resiliency Overlay District. Specifically, the 
applicant proposes the demolition of the buildings at 24 Endicott Street (Map 25, 
Lot 595) and 56 Margin Street (Map 25, Lot 597), the adaptive reuse of 54 
Margin Street (Map 25, Lot 597), and the preservation of the façade of 20 
Endicott Street (Map 25, Lot 597) to accommodate for a 22,806 square foot 
building comprised of 53 affordable homes, a shelter with 70 beds, and 
supportive programing space along with other site improvements. Thirteen 
parking spaces are proposed on site. 
 
Andrew Leonard is present for the Applicant and request a continuance to the 
September 17, 2026 Planning Board meeting. Mr. Leonard discusses that under 
the 40R zoning, the 120-day time limit will expire on October 9, 2026 and that 
the team is open to a 30-day extension. Ms. Cunningham says that the extension 
would bring the project to the first meeting in November. Mr. Leonard believes a 
45-day extension would be better then.  
 
Planning Board Comment 
 
None 
 
A motion to continue to the September 17, 2026 regular Planning Board meeting is made by 
Jonathan Berk, seconded by Helen Sides, and passes 7-0 in a roll call vote with one abstention.

D. 25 Bow Street (Map 16, Lot 32) and (Map 15, Lot 129)  
Applicant: The Infinity Group Investments, LLC  
Description: A public hearing for all persons interested in the application of The 
Infinity Group Investments, LLC requesting a waiver of frontage requirements of 
the Subdivision Control Law located at 25 Bow Street (Map 16, Lot 32) and (Map 
15, Lot 129). 
 
Joseph Luna, Luna Design Group, is in attendance for the Applicant. Lesly 
Yankelevich, Infinity Group is also in attendance.  
 
Ms. Eimert recuses herself as she voted on this item when a member of the 
Zoning Board of Appeals (ZBA). 
 
The Applicant would like to subdivided the lot into two (2) parcels. The ZBA 
granted the relief required concerning frontage (Ord Street requires 100 feet 
where 93.36 feet are present) and lot size (15000 square feet where 6000 square 
feet are present). The Planning Board is only reviewing the frontage. 
 
Public Comment 
 
None 
 
Planning Board Comments 
 
Ms. Tarbet asks about the retaining wall along Ord Street. The Applicant will 
work on the grading for vehicular traffic. Access the parcel is along Ord Street.  
 
Ms. Cunningham shares the draft decision on screen.  
 
A motion to close the public hearing is made by Jonathan Berk, seconded by Helen Sides, and 
passes 7-0 in a roll call vote with one recusal (R).

F. 59 Boston (Map 15, Lot 321)  
Applicant: Pediatric Associates  
Description: A public hearing for all persons interested in the application of 
Pediatric Associates located at 59 Boston Street (Map 15, Lot 321) in the 
Business Highway (B2), Residential Multi-Family (R3), Entrance Corridor Overlay 
District (ECOD), and Coastal Resilience Overlay District (C-ROD) for Coastal 
Resilience Overlay District (C-ROD) Site Plan Review in accordance with Section 
8.9 of the Salem Zoning Ordinance. Specifically, the applicant proposes plan 
improvements in accordance with C-ROD, interior renovations, an increase in 
parking spaces, and site improvements for ECOD compliance. 
 
Bob Griffin, Griffin Engineering, is in attendance for the Applicant. Chris Vance, 
architect, and Mark McKenna, Pediatric Associates are also in attendance. 
 
Mr. Griffin shares his screen. The site is the former Walgreens and is being 
converted to a medical office building. The site is located in the C-ROD and is 
outside of the 500-year and 100-year Flood Zone. The C-ROD predictions are 
14.4 at Bridge Street to 14.0 at the rear of the property. The highest number 
elevation is fourteen and four tenths (14.4) in the footprint of the building. The 
building is thirteen thousand eight hundred (13800) square feet with fifty-four 
(54) existing parking spaces and three (3) entrances to the site. Current building 
elevation is thirteen and sixty-seven hundredths (13.67), or about six (6) inches 
below the C-ROD predictions and existing floor elevation.  
 
Site plan changes  include landscaping, clarifying a one-way travel path, adding a 
dumpster location along southeast corner, and closing off the Pope Street 
entrance. This will increase parking to sixty (60) spaces.  
 
The Applicant removed nine (9) dead trees and eighteen (18) will be planted. 
Perennials and shrubs will be added as well.  
 
Changes to the floor elevation due to the heavily reinforced concrete slab that 
the building is on. The proposed new use will need more waste water and 
plumbing work; cutting through reinforced concrete could cause a structural 
problem. The Applicant will raise the floor eighteen (18) inches allowing 
plumbing lines to be installed underneath. The thirteen and seven tenth (13.7) 
elevation is now fifteen and two tenths (15.2) and above the C-ROD elevation of   
fourteen and four tenths (14.4). Additionally, steps will be added to the entrance

as well as an ADA accessible ramp. Temporary barriers will be deployed in case 
of flooding.  
 
Public Comment 
 
None 
 
Planning Board Comment 
 
Ms. Sides hopes that the team studies the actual number of  parking spaces they 
will need; the number planned is excessive. More greenery would be better. She 
hopes the design work achieves a better looking building to keep it from looking 
like a Walgreens. Ms. Tarbet reminds that they are looking at C-ROD, not design. 
 
Mr. Rieder clarifies that vegetation, and screening is within the purview of the 
board. He only sees sizes, not quantities of the proposed landscaping. Are the 
size calipers below the minimum? Mr. Griffin says they are replacing trees; he 
feels that if they put larger trees they would need to plant less. He was told 
smaller trees may plant better. Mr. Rieder agrees, however, if the ECOD 
stipulates x, which is his question. Curious why there is no tree in the corner of 
Pope Street and Boston Street? How can they get another tree there? Why is the 
dumpster pad spanning the property line? Mr. Griffin reiterates that it is an 
internal property line. 
Ms. Cunningham says the ECOD max caliper is four (4), and min is one and a half 
(1.5) and for C-ROD, info about landscaping is required and landscaping can be 
commented on if it relates to C-ROD, for example for minimization of 
utilities/engineering best practices. 
Ms. Tarbet agrees with Ms. Sides on the parking. Mr. Griffin says that a 
reevaluation could happen after the site is operational. Mr. McKenna was 
leaving it as is. Mr. Rieder refers to the C-ROD site plan review; Ms. Cunningham 
says that the review criteria are under section 8.9.10. Ms. Cunningham shares 
her screen to discuss the ECOD requirements. Mr. Rieder says that the Applicant 
cut down trees; Mr. Griffin states that the Applicant did not know about the tree 
ordinance and only removed dead trees. Additionally, he does not believe that a 
portion of the site being in the ECOD should be reason to install new landscaping 
beds throughout the site as it does create an extraordinary cost. Mr. Rieder 
concurs and wants to make certain that the proper number of trees at the 
proper size are planted and that he would be happy with the addition of one 
tree. The Applicant is happy to add.

A motion to continue to the September 17, 2026 regular Planning Board meeting is made by Kirt

G. 75 North Street (Map 26, Lot 58), 3 South Mason Street (Map 26, Lot 54), and 2 
Commercial Street (Map 26, Lot 57)  
Applicant: 75 North Street LLC  
Description: A public hearing for all persons interested in the application of 75 
North Street LLC located at 75 North Street (Map 26, Lot 58), 3 South Mason 
Street (Map 26, Lot 54), and 2 Commercial Street (Map 26, Lot 57) in the North
City of Salem Planning Board

River Canal Corridor (NRCC), Entrance Corridor Overlay District (ECOD), Flood 
Hazard Overlay District (FHOD), and Coastal Resilience Overlay District (C-ROD) 
for C-ROD Site Plan Review in accordance with Section 8.9 of the Salem Zoning 
Ordinance. Specifically, the Applicant proposes to implement flood-proofing 
measures in accordance with Section 8.9 of the Salem Zoning Ordinance to the 
previously approved multifamily residential building. 
 
Bob Griffin, Griffin Engineering and Dan Skolski, DMS Design, are present for the 
Applicant.  
 
Mr. Griffin shares his screen. The plan went through the Planning Board process 
prior to the C-ROD taking effect. Have been through the MEPA process and 
through the Conservation Commission. Flood zone AE elevation ten (10). The 
new elevation, C-ROD fourteen and four tenths (14.4) highest in building 
footprint. There are no significant changes to the plan.  
 
Public Comment 
 
none 
 
Planning Board Comments 
 
Ms. Sides is curious to know if the project has changed hands and whether there 
have been changes in materials approved. Mr. Skolski says there is no change in 
ownership, and the only material change is on the interior – fiberglass drywall as 
opposed to the usual.  
 
Mr. Furey thinks the entire project is a public safety hazard, with entering and 
exiting on North Street. Also concerned with insurance for residents with the 
flooding. Opposed to it going any further.  
 
Mr. Rieder was confused by the staff memo. Ms. Cunningham clarifies that as 
listed in the zoning, there can't be a decision made on this until the Planning 
Board has heard from the necessary departments or until 35 has passed, that is 
September 15. In terms of the Engineering comment, if the Board wants to wait 
longer than the September 15 date, the engineering comment shouldn’t be the 
reason unless it impacts C-ROD. Mr. Griffin says it has no effect.  
 
Mr. Berk says that the sewage plan has changed and that may be why 
engineering says that they shouldn’t approve. Mr. Griffin says the change isn’t 
inconsistent with site plan review. They had moved the sewer part of plans all

along. It seems that this doesn’t apply to C-ROD. Ms. Tarbet is interested in the 
Director of Sustainability’s comments.  
 
Mr. Rieder says “planning board shall not until…” precluding the Board from 
voting tonight.  
 
Ms. Eimert is curious if the Applicant can share the design elements pertinent to 
pedestrian safety (tenant safety in a flood event). Mr. Griffin says that when we 
get extreme flooding, the building manager will communicate the tenants move 
their cars to higher ground. When the waters do come in, the residents will be at 
elevation 23 and safer at that higher elevation. There are higher walkways and 
grades at the South Mason Street side. 8.5 at North Street, so it is more difficult. 
Ms. Eimert clarifies that utilities are elevated outside the flood standard.

Applicant: Bohler Engineering f/b/o Prime Storage Shetland LLC c/o Prime Group 
Holdings, LLC  
Description: Form B/Preliminary Subdivision Application 
 
The Applicant is not in attendance. 
 
Mr. Furey would like this project to be in front of a massive meeting with all the boards.  
 
Mr. Rieder doesn’t think they should continue the item as the Applicant couldn’t be 
bothered to show. Mr. Berk agrees.  
 
Ms. Cunningham says that there is no legal consequence if the Board does not take 
action in forty five (45) days. Mr. Berk would like the City Solicitor’s opinion. 
 
III. OLD AND NEW BUSINESS

A. Review and Comment – Mass Wildlife Update 
 
Mass Wildlife submitted a letter asking for Board comments on the letter’s content. 
Comment period until October 4, 2026.  
 
B. Other  
 
Mr. Rieder checked on the 160 Federal Street enclosure, and it is still there. He is 
curious as to how the board didn’t review it. Ms. Cunningham says that it was not 
approved, it was just built by the Applicant. They are looking for a Certificate of 
Occupancy (CO), but Ms. Cunningham hasn’t signed off on it because of this 
structure and other changes that have been made. Mr. Rieder is sending Ms. 
Cunningham photos. Ms. Tarbet asks what is typically done in a situation like this. 
Ms. Cunningham says that the project can submit for an amendment if they want to 
keep/rebuild the structure and she would provide a recommendation to the 
director. It is on the Applicant to let the city know if they want to rebuild or seek an 
amendment.  
 
Regarding Form B,  it is 45-days of submission date which was August 14 (October 8 
would be day 45). Mr. Berk says they saw this on Bertini’s with the freezing of the 
zoning. Ms. Cunningham says that filing of preliminary plan says that a freeze occurs 
with a definitive plan within seven (7) months.
